requirement:
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.

A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. The tests I weighed are all marked `{test}` for it. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

1. **Only fresh results with compatible build configurations contribute counts.**
   - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` first checks that fresh results for tests "one" and "two" give the expected line-count union. It then records a new "one" result under a different configuration (`build-b`). It asserts that only that one result is selected, so the older `build-a` results are excluded.
   - `fn[stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals]` shows that a fresh run passes with `code.rs: 2/2 (100.0%)`.

2. **Changed inputs make a result stale and exclude it from totals.**
   - The filtered-run test edits `code.rs` and asserts every record is `!fresh` and the check reports `stale coverage`.
   - The `...publish_no_current_file_totals` test asserts the stale report has no `- code.rs:` totals and no `100.0%`.
   - `src/execution_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_and_build_inputs_invalidate_on_addition_removal_and_dirty_content]` calls `fresh()` directly. It covers these changes:
     - edited, added and removed source files;
     - `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` edited, and removed;
     - a member manifest and `rust-toolchain.toml` added;
     - watched generated inputs, including a non-Rust file under `node_modules` and a path that did not exist before.
     It also checks that restoring each input makes the result fresh again.
   - `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_build_captures_dependency_files_and_environment_for_read_only_freshness_checks]` is an end-to-end check with a real build. It confirms dependency-file and environment captures, then changes `include_str!` data, a `build.rs` rerun input, and the compiler and build environment variables. Each change makes the saved check report `stale coverage`. Restoring each input clears the staleness, and the stored files are unchanged afterwards.
   - `book.rs#fn[cargo_launch_metadata_does_not_invalidate_but_caller_build_environment_does]` checks build-configuration compatibility. Launch-only Cargo values do not invalidate a result. Changes to `CC`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_PROFILE_*`, a target linker variable and a fixture build input do.

3. **Results of unknown compatibility are identified as unavailable and excluded.**
   - The `...publish_no_current_file_totals` test sets the run schema to an unsupported value. It asserts the check fails with "cannot establish the current test set" and that there are no totals.
   - `fn[unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success]` covers four cases: corrupt metadata, missing captured source, unsupported schema, and a missing profile. Each fails the check, and an older success does not come back with positive counts.
   - The filtered-run test also covers `failed` and `interrupted` newest attempts. Both give a failing check that reports "missing or unreadable coverage".

4. **A filtered run preserves provenance and does not make unselected results fresh.**
   - `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_recollection_leaves_only_the_unselected_result_stale_with_its_original_sources]` re-records only "rerun" after a source change. It asserts these things:
     - "unselected" is reported stale and "rerun" is not.
     - There are no totals.
     - The preserved record keeps its original attempt id, run id and captured source (`fn a() {}`).
     - The re-run record carries the new source.
   - The `...publish_no_current_file_totals` test asserts the SQLite store and the `.profraw` report still exist after the stale and unknown states. The filtered-run test asserts the captured source is retained.

**Assessment**

I found no named boundary or failure case without a test, and the assertions check the required outcomes. Cargo configuration files are not varied in any test I reviewed, but the requirement does not name them as a distinct case, so I do not count that as a gap. The cited `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and `requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace` are context only, and I did not reassess them.

text: :::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
